questions.stem: What is a listing in Snowflake?

options.text: A physical copy of a database sent to a consumer
An enhanced method of Secure Data Sharing that uses the same provider and consumer model
A replication group for disaster recovery
A type of virtual warehouse for sharing compute

explanation.correct: A listing is an enhanced method of Secure Data Sharing that uses the same provider and consumer model, adding capabilities like Marketplace publishing, monetization, usage metrics, and metadata.

distractors.A: Listings do not copy data; they build on Secure Data Sharing (no data copied).
distractors.C: A listing is not a replication group; replication is a business-continuity feature.
distractors.D: A listing is not a warehouse; it is a data-sharing construct.

questions.stem: In listing terminology, what is a 'data product'?

options.text: The consumer's virtual warehouse
A Marketplace invoice
The share or the app attached to your listing
A reader account

explanation.correct: A data product is the share or the Snowflake Native App attached to your listing.

distractors.A: The consumer's warehouse is compute, not the data product.
distractors.B: An invoice is a billing artifact, not the data product.
distractors.D: A reader account is a sharing mechanism, not the data product attached to a listing.

questions.stem: What are the two availability options when offering a listing?

options.text: Inbound or outbound
Free or paid only
Regional or global only
Privately (to specific consumers) or publicly (on the Snowflake Marketplace)

explanation.correct: When offering a listing you choose to make the data product available privately (only to specific consumers) or publicly (visible on the Snowflake Marketplace).

distractors.A: Inbound/outbound describes share direction, not listing availability options.
distractors.B: Free/paid are access options, not the availability (private vs public) choice.
distractors.C: Regional/global is not how listing availability is categorized.

questions.stem: Which THREE access options can a provider choose for how consumers access a listing's data product? (Select THREE)

options.text: Anonymous access with no account required
Read-write access to the provider's base tables
Free access to the full data product
Limited trial access, with full access on request
Paid access using Snowflake pricing models
Time-limited write access

explanation.correct: The access options are free access to the full data product, limited trial access (with full access available on request), and paid access using Snowflake's pricing models.

distractors.A: Consumers access listings through Snowflake accounts; there is no anonymous no-account access.
distractors.B: Listings never grant read-write access to a provider's base tables.
distractors.F: There is no time-limited write-access option for listings.

questions.stem: Which TWO capabilities do listings add on top of basic Secure Data Sharing? (Select TWO)

options.text: Copy data physically into the consumer account
Grant consumers OWNERSHIP of shared objects
Offer a share publicly on the Snowflake Marketplace
Charge consumers for access to the data
Eliminate all compute costs for consumers

explanation.correct: Listings add capabilities such as offering a share publicly on the Snowflake Marketplace and charging consumers for access (plus usage monitoring and metadata).

distractors.A: Listings build on Secure Data Sharing, which does not copy data.
distractors.B: Consumers never receive OWNERSHIP of shared objects.
distractors.E: Consumers still pay for compute; listings don't eliminate compute costs.

questions.scenario: A provider wants to publish a generic, aggregated dataset that any Marketplace consumer can access instantly at no cost.
questions.stem: A provider wants a generic aggregated dataset available instantly at no cost on the Marketplace. Which TWO statements about free listings are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A free listing requires the consumer to pay before access
A free listing provides instant access to the full published dataset
A free listing can be offered publicly on the Marketplace or privately to specific consumers
A free listing only provides a limited subset of data
A free listing grants consumers write access

explanation.correct: A free listing provides instant access to the full published dataset and can be offered publicly on the Marketplace or privately to specific consumers.

distractors.D: Free listings provide the full dataset, not a limited subset (that is a trial).

questions.scenario: A provider wants to make a data product visible and free-to-try to anyone on the Marketplace, but grant full access only to consumers they choose.
questions.stem: A provider wants a data product free-to-try by anyone on the Marketplace but full access only for chosen consumers. Which TWO statements about limited trial listings are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It grants full unlimited access to everyone immediately
It is only ever offered privately to a single consumer
It makes a product visible and free to try by anyone on the Marketplace
Full access is available only to consumers the provider chooses to do business with
It cannot be used for customer-specific data

explanation.correct: A limited trial listing makes a product visible and free to try by anyone on the Marketplace, but full access is available only to consumers the provider chooses to do business with.

distractors.A: It grants limited access, not full unlimited access to everyone.
distractors.B: It is available on the Marketplace to anyone to try, not private to one consumer.
distractors.E: It is well-suited to customer-specific data and licensing-restricted cases.

questions.scenario: A provider is configuring a limited trial listing and must set how long the trial data product is available.
questions.stem: What is the allowed availability period range for a limited trial listing?

options.text: 1 to 30 days
1 to 90 days
7 to 60 days
Unlimited

explanation.correct: Providers can set the availability period for limited trial listings from 1 to 90 days.

distractors.C: The range is 1 to 90 days, not 7 to 60.
distractors.D: The trial period is bounded (1 to 90 days), not unlimited.

questions.scenario: A provider responds to a consumer's request for full access after a limited trial.
questions.stem: Which TWO options can the provider offer in response? (Select TWO)

options.text: A free private listing (e.g., for an existing business relationship or negotiated terms)
A paid private listing using a Snowflake pricing model
Direct write access to the provider's production tables
A reader account with unlimited free compute for the consumer
Automatic ownership transfer of the dataset

explanation.correct: In response to a full-access request, a provider might offer a free private listing (e.g., existing relationship/negotiated terms) or a paid private listing using one of Snowflake's pricing models.

distractors.C: Listings never grant write access to provider tables.
distractors.D: A reader account is unrelated to fulfilling a trial-to-full request and would bill the provider for compute.
distractors.E: There is no automatic ownership transfer of the dataset.

questions.scenario: A provider wants to offer several SKUs for one paid listing without creating a separate listing for each SKU.
questions.stem: Which feature enables this?

options.text: Pricing plans (with offers extended to consumers)
Auto-fulfillment
Reader accounts
Data Exchange

explanation.correct: Pricing plans allow providers to offer multiple SKUs for a single paid listing. After creating a pricing plan, providers create offers extended to consumers (with individualized billing, terms, and dates).

distractors.B: Auto-fulfillment replicates data products across regions; it does not manage SKUs.
distractors.C: Reader accounts are for non-Snowflake consumers, not SKU management.
distractors.D: A Data Exchange manages a group of accounts, not multiple SKUs on one listing.

questions.scenario: A provider evaluates regional availability constraints before creating a paid listing.
questions.stem: Which statement about paid listings is correct?

options.text: They are available in all regions without restriction
They can only be offered privately, never on the Marketplace
They are available to consumers and from providers only in specific regions
They require the consumer to own the provider account

explanation.correct: Paid listings are only available to consumers in specific regions, and from providers in specific regions.

distractors.A: Paid listings are region-restricted, not universally available.
distractors.B: Paid listings can be offered privately or on the Marketplace.
distractors.D: Consumers do not need to own the provider account.

questions.stem: Which THREE types of metadata can a provider include with a listing to help consumers? (Select THREE)

options.text: The consumer's account password
The provider's cloud billing credentials
A title
A description
Sample SQL queries
The consumer's private encryption keys

explanation.correct: Listings let providers include metadata such as a title, description, sample SQL queries, and information about the data provider.

distractors.A: A consumer's password is never part of listing metadata.
distractors.B: Cloud billing credentials are not listing metadata.
distractors.F: Encryption keys are never included as listing metadata.

questions.scenario: A provider wants to understand how consumers engage with a published listing.
questions.stem: Which listing capability supports this?

options.text: Directly reading the consumer's query history tables
Monitoring interest in the listing and usage of the data in the share
Logging into the consumer account
Modifying the consumer's warehouse settings

explanation.correct: Listings let providers monitor interest in their listing and usage of the data in the share (consumer usage metrics).

distractors.A: Providers cannot directly read consumer query history tables.
distractors.C: Providers cannot log into consumer accounts.
distractors.D: Providers cannot modify consumer warehouse settings.

questions.scenario: A team wants to use listings and the Snowflake Marketplace for the first time.
questions.stem: What is required before doing so?

options.text: Agree to additional terms (legal requirements for providers and consumers of listings)
Upgrade to Business Critical Edition
Create a reader account first
Disable role-based access control

explanation.correct: To use listings and the Snowflake Marketplace, you need to agree to additional terms (the legal requirements for providers and consumers of listings).

distractors.B: Business Critical is not required to use listings/Marketplace.
distractors.C: A reader account is not a prerequisite for using listings.
distractors.D: RBAC is not disabled to use listings.

questions.scenario: A provider evaluates why using a Marketplace listing might be better than maintaining individual direct shares with many consumers.
questions.stem: Which TWO advantages does a Marketplace listing provide? (Select TWO)

options.text: Guarantee zero compute cost for the provider
Share curated data offerings with many consumers simultaneously
Optionally charge for data products with paid listings
Automatically grant write access to consumers
Bypass the need for consumer Snowflake accounts

explanation.correct: A Marketplace listing lets a provider share curated offerings with many consumers at once (instead of per-consumer relationships) and, with paid listings, charge for data products.

distractors.A: Listings do not guarantee zero provider compute cost.
distractors.D: Listings never grant write access to consumers.
distractors.E: Consumers still need Snowflake accounts to access Marketplace listings.

questions.scenario: A provider offers a listing containing a Snowflake Native App rather than a plain dataset.
questions.stem: Is this supported, and what can the app include?

options.text: No; listings can only contain raw tables
Yes, but only non-secure views
No; apps must be shared as direct shares
Yes; a listing can share a Snowflake Native App (business logic like Streamlit apps, procedures, and functions), free or paid

explanation.correct: A provider can share a Snowflake Native App via a listing (free or paid). The app's business logic can include a Streamlit app, stored procedures, and functions.

distractors.A: Listings can contain a Native App as the data product, not just raw tables.
distractors.B: Apps include business logic, not merely views.
distractors.C: Apps are distributed via listings, not direct shares.

questions.scenario: A consumer accesses a listing on the Snowflake Marketplace to explore providers and data products.
questions.stem: Through which Snowflake interface do consumers explore listings and providers on the Marketplace?

options.text: SnowSQL only
Snowsight
The classic reader-account console
A resource monitor dashboard

explanation.correct: Consumers explore listings and providers on the Snowflake Marketplace through Snowsight.

distractors.A: The Marketplace exploration experience is in Snowsight, not exclusively SnowSQL.
distractors.C: There is no classic reader-account console for Marketplace exploration.
distractors.D: A resource monitor dashboard governs credits, not Marketplace exploration.

questions.scenario: A provider compares free listings versus limited trial listings for different data types.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements correctly contrast these listing types? (Select TWO)

options.text: A free listing provides instant access to the full published dataset
A limited trial listing provides instant limited access, with full access available on request
A free listing requires payment before any access
A limited trial listing grants full unlimited access immediately
Both types can only be offered privately, never publicly

explanation.correct: A free listing gives instant access to the full dataset, while a limited trial listing gives instant limited access with full access available on request.

distractors.C: A free listing requires no payment.
distractors.D: A limited trial grants limited access, not full unlimited access immediately.
distractors.E: Free listings can be private or public; limited trial listings are available on the Marketplace.

questions.scenario: A provider wants unified procurement so consumers can try and then buy a proprietary data product through Snowflake.
questions.stem: Which listing type best supports this try-and-buy, proprietary-data use case?

options.text: Free listing
Organizational listing
Paid listing
Non-secure direct share

explanation.correct: Paid listings are best for proprietary or industry-specific data and offer consumers the ability to try and buy a data product with unified procurement through Snowflake.

distractors.A: A free listing does not involve buying or unified procurement.
distractors.B: Organizational listings are for internal sharing, not commercial try-and-buy.
distractors.D: A non-secure direct share is not a listing and offers no procurement.

questions.scenario: A provider extends a specific paid offer to a consumer with individualized billing, payment terms, and contract start/end dates.
questions.stem: What is this construct called?

options.text: A secure share area
A release directive
A data exchange
An offer (created from a pricing plan)

explanation.correct: An offer (created from a pricing plan) provides consumers with individualized billing, payment terms, payment schedules, and contract start and end dates, which the consumer can review, accept, or reject.

distractors.A: A secure share area (SSA) is an auto-fulfillment construct, not a billing offer.
distractors.B: A release directive points to an app version/patch, unrelated to billing.
distractors.C: A data exchange manages a group of accounts, not an individualized paid offer.
